title: Partial-Quasi-Newton Methods: Efficient Algorithms for Minimax Optimization Problems with Unbalanced Dimensionality

problem.claim: The paper studies strongly-convex-strongly-concave minimax optimization problems with unbalanced dimensionality.

gap.claim: Conventional minimax optimization algorithms typically minimize total oracle calls while ignoring the unequal computational costs of accessing information from the two variables.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a Partial-Quasi-Newton method that exploits unbalanced problem structure to construct Hessian estimates efficiently.
The paper provides a convergence result showing that the proposed method reaches the saddle point faster than existing minimax optimization algorithms.
The paper reports numerical experiments on real-world applications comparing the proposed method with state-of-the-art methods.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present Partial-Quasi-Newton as a novel second-order optimization algorithm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the proposed method converges to the saddle point faster than existing minimax optimization algorithms.
The authors report that numerical experiments on real-world applications show significantly better performance than state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: The study concerns strongly-convex-strongly-concave minimax optimization with unbalanced dimensionality.
The problem setting is associated with applications including few-shot learning and fairness-aware machine learning.
Existing iterative algorithm design emphasizes total oracle calls but overlooks unequal computational costs for the two variables.
The authors propose the Partial-Quasi-Newton method, which uses the unbalanced structure to estimate the Hessian efficiently.
The abstract reports faster convergence theoretically and stronger performance in numerical experiments.

source_observation.claim: When variables have unequal information-access costs, minimizing total oracle calls may overlook the relevant computational bottleneck.

interpretation.claim: Algorithm design should account for variable-specific access costs in addition to counting oracle calls.

application.claim: For optimization problems with asymmetric variable dimensions or access costs, evaluate methods using cost-aware complexity measures and consider asymmetric second-order updates.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this lesson applies beyond strongly-convex-strongly-concave minimax problems with unbalanced dimensionality.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the algorithm's update rules or Hessian-estimation procedure.
The abstract does not provide convergence rates, complexity bounds, or experimental numerical results.
The abstract does not identify the real-world datasets, baselines, or evaluation settings.
